Newborn
NEW-born
adj. (recently born; newly brought forth)
Greek artigennetos, from arti, just now, and gennao, to beget or bring forth — just-born. The compound occurs once in the New Testament, and it is a figure for believers, not for infants.

Biblical Definition

As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby. Peter has just said what makes the figure fit: being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever. Because regeneration is a real birth, the newly regenerate are really newborn, and the appetite proper to a newborn is the one Peter commands. The comparison presses at three points. A newborn's hunger is instinctive and urgent, not cultivated. It is undiscriminating about everything except its object — milk, and nothing else will do. And it is aimed at growth, which is the reason the appetite exists. Sincere here means unadulterated, unmixed, without additive; the same concern Paul shows when he refuses to handle the word of God deceitfully. Peter is commanding a desire for the word itself, undiluted, and giving the reason plainly: that ye may grow thereby. The verse also settles a question about the Christian life at its start. The new birth is God's work, not the believer's — except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. But the growth that follows comes by an appointed food, and the newborn is commanded to want it. The next verse gives the ground of the appetite: if so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): recently born; as a newborn infant. NEW, lately made, invented, produced or come into being.

expand to see more

NEWBORN, a. Recently born; as a newborn infant.

NEW, a. Lately made, invented, produced, or come into being; that has existed a short time only.

BABE, n. An infant; a young child of either sex.

SINCERE, a. Pure; unmixed; unadulterated; as sincere milk; sincere doctrine.

MILK, n. A white fluid secreted for the nourishment of the young; figuratively, the first and plainest doctrine.

Key Scripture

1 Peter 2:2 — "As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby:"

1 Peter 1:23 — "Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God, which liveth and abideth for ever."

John 3:3 — "Jesus answered and said unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God."

1 Peter 2:3 — "If so be ye have tasted that the Lord is gracious."

Modern Corruption

The new birth is widely reduced to a decision the sinner makes, and the milk of the word to whatever a reader finds edifying; Peter makes regeneration God's act by his word and the milk the unadulterated word itself.

expand to see more

Where regeneration is treated as the sinner's own decision, the figure of a newborn collapses, because no infant begets itself. Peter is explicit about the agency and the instrument: born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God. The Reformed doctrine of the effectual call is not an imposition on these texts; it is what they say. The Lord told Nicodemus that a man must be born again to see the kingdom at all, which places the new birth before sight, not after choice. A gospel invitation is rightly pressed on every hearer, and the dictionary presses it; but the life that answers is given, not generated.

The second corruption is gentler and nearly universal: the sincere milk of the word read as any spiritual nourishment a believer happens to find sustaining — a devotional, a conference, a moving song. Sincere means unmixed, and the genitive is of the word. Peter is not commending an appetite for religious material; he is commanding hunger for Scripture itself, unadulterated. A church that substitutes commentary on the word for the word has quietly weaned its newborns, and the growth Peter promises comes only thereby.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek artigennetos (G738), newborn; anagennao (G313), to beget again; adolos (G97), without guile or adulteration; logikos (G3050), of the word.

expand to see more

Greek artigennetos (G738) — just-born; rendered newborn, its only occurrence.

Greek anagennao (G313) — to beget again; used by Peter alone, of God begetting his people.

Greek adolos (G97) — unadulterated, without guile; rendered sincere, the negative of doloo, to adulterate.

Greek logikos (G3050) — of the word, rational; the milk is the word's own.

Greek auxano (G837) — to grow; the purpose for which the appetite is commanded.

Usage

"“as newborn babes” — the figure follows the fact of regeneration."

"“the sincere milk of the word” — unmixed, with no additive."

"“that ye may grow thereby” — the appointed means of growth."
